title: Unique Binary Search Trees II Problem

content.problemStatement: You receive an integer `n`, output *all the structurally unique **BST'**s (binary search trees), which has exactly* `n` *nodes of unique values from* `1` *to* `n`. The task is to output the answer in **any order**.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: For this input, applying the required rules of Unique Binary Search Trees II produces [[1,null,2,null,3],[1,null,3,2],[2,1,3],[3,1,null,null,2],[3,2,null,1]].
For this input, applying the required rules of Unique Binary Search Trees II produces [[1]].

hints: Identify the search space and verify that the condition is monotonic (true...true...false...false).
Be mindful of integer overflow when computing mid: use mid = left + (right - left) // 2.
Ensure the termination condition (left <= right vs left < right) correctly handles boundary elements.
learningObjectives: Master core algorithmic concepts and pattern recognition for Unique Binary Search Trees II Problem.
Analyze time and space complexity trade-offs to meet optimal constraint benchmarks.
Formulate robust solutions addressing edge cases including boundary values and empty sets.
